# Copilot instructions

## Project shape

This is a TanStack Start application for an AI-native publishing workspace for technical blogs. The product direction in `AGENTS.md` and `design.md` matters: preserve author control, Git-friendly content workflows, reviewable AI changes, and a calm writing-focused UI rather than turning the app into a generic CMS.

The app is currently a client-side prototype:

- `src/routes/` contains TanStack Router file-based routes. `src/routes/__root.tsx` owns the document shell, metadata, global CSS, theme provider, and development tools.
- `src/components/` contains shared layout, editor, and UI primitives. `src/components/notion-editor.tsx` is the Lexical rich-text editor; it converts between Lexical state and Markdown and supports Markdown shortcuts.
- `src/components/article-editor.tsx` coordinates title/content/topic/status editing, save state, slug generation, keyboard save, and article persistence.
- `src/lib/blog-store.ts` is the domain model and persistence layer. It defines `Article` and the health/SEO/AEO/diff types, seeds sample articles, computes derived article intelligence, and stores data in `localStorage` under `blog_changer_articles_v1`. Browser-only access is guarded for SSR.
- Article list, reader, and editor flows are `/blogs`, `/blog/$id`, `/blog/$id/edit`, and `/new`. The `/blog/` route redirects to `/blogs`.
- `src/routeTree.gen.ts` is generated by TanStack Router. Add or change route files, then regenerate it; do not hand-edit the generated file.

There is no server/database/API integration yet. Do not describe `localStorage` data as durable backend storage or add server assumptions without implementing the corresponding integration.

## Commands

Run these from the repository root:

```bash
npm install
npm run dev              # Vite dev server on port 3000
npm run build            # production Vite/Nitro build
npm run preview          # serve the production build
npm run generate-routes  # regenerate src/routeTree.gen.ts after route changes
npm run lint             # ESLint
npm run check            # Prettier check
npm run format           # Prettier write followed by ESLint --fix
```

There is currently no test script, test runner, or checked-in test suite, so there is no single-test command. Use `npm run build` for the repository's production/type-oriented validation and `npm run lint` for static checks.

## Implementation conventions

- Use the `#/` alias for imports from `src` (for example `#/components/ui/button` and `#/lib/blog-store`). Keep route imports compatible with TanStack's generated route tree.
- Define routes with `createFileRoute(...)`; use route params/search validation from the route object rather than reading `window.location` manually.
- Keep article mutations centralized in `BlogStore`. Use its save/delete/diff methods and derived metric helpers instead of writing directly to `localStorage` from page components.
- Treat `Article` as the shared contract for article metadata and intelligence. When adding article fields, update the type, seed data/default construction, persistence normalization, and any relevant editor/list/reader surfaces together.
- `BlogStore` is synchronous and browser-backed. Keep reads safe during SSR (`typeof window !== 'undefined'`) and preserve the seed fallback behavior.
- The editor's source of truth is Markdown content even though editing is visual. Preserve Markdown round-tripping through Lexical transformers and keep meaningful AI/content changes represented as reviewable diffs.
- Use existing UI primitives under `src/components/ui/` before adding one-off controls. Follow the existing `cn(...)` class composition pattern.
- Styling uses Tailwind CSS v4 plus tokens in `src/styles.css`. The visual system is warm stone/off-white with electric indigo as the primary accent, Geist/Geist Mono for UI, and Lora for display text. Preserve light/dark theme support through `ThemeProvider`.
- Formatting is configured in `prettier.config.js`: no semicolons, single quotes, and trailing commas. TypeScript is strict with unused locals/parameters disallowed.
- Keep `routeTree.gen.ts`, build output, and other generated artifacts out of manual edits. ESLint intentionally ignores generated route/build directories.

## UI/product constraints

Keep the article as the visual focus: minimal controls, restrained panels, contextual intelligence, and reversible/reviewable suggestions. Avoid generic dashboard clutter, gratuitous gradients/animations, or AI actions that silently rewrite content. For product-level decisions, consult `AGENTS.md`; for visual tokens and layout direction, consult `design.md`.
